findings.reason: The protected Python solution implements read(buf, n) by repeatedly invoking read4(temporary) until n characters are copied or the file ends. It caps each transfer at min(available, n - copied), properly handling early file termination and sub-chunk bounds. The solution runs in O(n) time and O(1) space; no candidate is required.

Iteratively consuming read4 into a 4-character temporary buffer and copying min(available, n - copied) guarantees that exactly min(n, file_length) characters are read in order into buf without out-of-bounds writes.
Making at most ceil(min(n, file_length) / 4) + 1 calls to read4 takes O(n) time. Auxiliary space is O(1) for the 4-character temporary buffer. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts destination buffer buf (List[str]) and integer n, populating buf in-place and returning the integer count of actual characters read.

The approach accurately details 4-character primitive buffer consumption, min(available, n - copied) copy capping, end-of-file zero/short read detection, and O(n) time / O(1) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover single read4 call limits, uncapped chunk copy buffer overrun risks, surplus character persistence irrelevance for single-call contracts, file shorter than n EOF handling, n < 4 partial chunk copying, and exact multiple-of-4 file boundary behavior.

App Python and native Python solutions both execute the identical 4-character buffer read4 consumption algorithm with SHA-256 digests 932dfa02abbf8e45482d2f259429025296160c548c2b901ea769a236b9b7c8c1 and 2da3401b0a595596c4fd8427c2c092157383d9cd49eb6aa15ee80a4831a5a9a4.
